# EII — Complete Scientific Reference Register

**Document version:** 0.3.1 · Local review draft · 21 October 2026
**Work in Progress — Academic Research Resource**
Jonathan Minchin · Ecological Interaction · ORCID 0000-0001-8152-1796.

This is the authoritative machine-oriented scientific register for the [human-readable Scientific Reference Register](EII_Scientific_Reference_Register.md). It retains all 235 indicators, 15 domains, full canonical and display descriptions, classifications, supporting relationships, references, candidate source routes and observation schemas. Stable IDs have not been renamed or consolidated.

## Format and interpretation

Each indicator has one JSON object in a fenced `json` block beneath its stable anchor. The first block is the document manifest; indicator blocks have a top-level `id`; the final block contains explicitly labelled historical context. Markdown is the container, not a standalone JSON file. Parse the JSON fences and distinguish their roles before importing.

Existing record fields are preserved. Additive `historical_*` fields retain earlier full-length inventory text and exact earlier table rows, including the original v0.1.0 descriptions for its 120 records. Historical wording is source evidence, not a second current definition. Historical context below preserves the earlier schemas, bibliographies, methodological cautions and presentation history. Its old file-role, installation and validation statements describe their source editions, not this revision.

The intended methodology reference is **Database Research Methodology (DRM) v1.0.0**. Its authoritative specification was unavailable for this revision; conformance is unverified. No DRM fields or validation results are invented. Existing EII schemas are retained rather than replaced with the illustrative schema from the planning discussion.

EII remains scientific and technological. Trails4Soil practice crosswalks and interoperability dependencies on PBCKA/EIRKB remain excluded. GISDS catalogue resources are candidate acquisition routes, not bound observations; AMRKB supplies potential technical-method context. Future IoT and bioinformatics bindings retain null identifiers. Measurements, inferred properties and interpretation remain distinct. Entries are working definitions, not verified monitoring standards.

## Domain taxonomy and migration

**Classification reference:** EII Domain Taxonomy v1.0.0. The existing `domain` field is the primary scientific domain; `related_domains` retains secondary scientific-domain relationships. The D01–D15 codes are stable identifiers, independent of document order and indicator prefixes. The code-to-label definitions and verified counts are recorded in the manifest.

All 235 existing primary assignments and all 72 existing secondary-domain relationships are preserved. This migration reorganises the Scientific Reference Register's A–P presentation groups; it does not introduce new scientific domain assertions. The manifest's `classification_migration.crosswalk` maps every stable EII ID from its previous scientific presentation group to its primary and secondary domains. The former document manifest and earlier introductions are retained as historical provenance. Historical file paths, source hashes and archived prose still describe their source editions.

The taxonomy version is separate from this document version, the scientific/remote document versions, `eii.reference-register/1.0`, DRM v1.0.0 and any future resource release. DRM conformance remains unverified until the authoritative methodology specification is available.

## Version history

- **0.3.1 — 2026-10-21:** Adopted EII Domain Taxonomy v1.0.0 as the explicit shared classification reference; added the 235-ID A–P migration crosswalk and per-record taxonomy reference. Preserved all existing record fields/values and historical content, corrected current file-role metadata and the scientific-register link, and retained the prior manifest/introduction. No primary or secondary domain assignments changed.
- **0.3.0 — 2026-10-19:** Authoritative structured register with 235 indicators, full scientific/display fields, source registries and additive historical preservation fields. Earlier edition details remain in the source context.

## Classifications

The 15 domains organise the main register. This table adds how the indicator is obtained, the scales where it is commonly used, and its ecological purpose.

The listed scales are guides. A soil sample, sensor reading and satellite pixel represent different areas and times; they need suitable methods before being compared. Genetic potential, gene expression and actual process rates also remain different kinds of evidence.

## Observation methods and information products

| Method / platform | Primary observations or products | Typical EII use | Main qualification |
|---|---|---|---|
| RGB drone, camera or orthophoto | Visible colour channels and mapped surface features | Vegetation cover, terraces, built geometry | Lighting, colour processing, scale and geometric accuracy affect comparisons. |
| Multispectral / hyperspectral sensing | Reflectance at specified wavelengths | Greenness, pigment and moisture contrasts; calibrated traits | Band ratios directly describe spectra; physiology requires validation. No hyperspectral dataset was bound from GISDS. |
| Thermal imaging | Thermal radiance and retrieved surface temperature | Surface heating and canopy temperature anomalies | Emissivity, atmosphere and acquisition time matter; surface temperature differs from air temperature. |
| Satellite radar (SAR) | Backscatter/coherence and interpreted classifications | Inundation and surface-change screening | Moisture, roughness, vegetation and viewing geometry can produce similar signals. |
| LiDAR / structure-from-motion | Point clouds, terrain and surface models | Height, crown geometry, terrain and repeat change | Ground classification, co-registration and occlusion affect results; geometry is not biomass directly. |
| Weather / hydrology stations and future IoT | Temperature, rainfall, humidity, flow and calibrated sensor streams | Climate, water balance, exposure and event monitoring | Record sensor calibration, depth/height, gaps, drift and temporal support. |
| Soil / water laboratory assays | Carbon, nutrients, chemistry and physical properties | Pools, concentrations, contamination and retention | Extraction, dry/wet basis, detection limits and compatible units must be declared. |
| Field ecological surveys | Organisms, abundance, traits, visits and demographic observations | Biodiversity, interactions and population change | Sampling effort and imperfect detection constrain inference. |
| Amplicon / shotgun sequencing | Marker sequences, taxonomic profiles and encoded genes | Community composition and genetic potential | Relative reads are not absolute abundance; DNA potential is not expression or process flux. |
| RNA, proteins and metabolites | Transcripts, detected proteins and metabolite pools | Biochemical state and activity-related evidence | These evidence layers remain distinct; pools/signals do not directly measure realised flux. |
| Controlled process assays / flux measurements | Transformation, growth, respiration or exchange rates | Nitrogen cycling, decomposition and carbon balances | Assay conditions and field representativeness determine applicability. |

## Source register

| Source ref | Resource / contribution | Interpretation note |
|---|---|---|
| RS001 | [Copernicus Browser](https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/) — Satellite imagery and indices | GeoTIFF; raw versus rendered export matters |
| RS002 | [USGS EarthExplorer](https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov/) — Landsat reflectance and temperature | Follow product scaling and quality masks |
| RS004 | [Copernicus Land Monitoring Service](https://land.copernicus.eu/en) — Land cover and environmental variables | Check resolution, period and product documentation |
| RS005 | [ESA WorldCover](https://viewer.esa-worldcover.org/) — 10 m land-cover maps: 2020 and 2021 | Algorithms differ between years; GeoTIFF and QGIS styles |
| RS006 | [Dynamic World](https://www.dynamicworld.app/) — 10 m land-cover classes and probabilities | Per-observation classification varies with conditions |
| RS009 | [MapBiomas](https://mapbiomas.org/) — Annual land-cover and land-use maps | Coverage, collections and methods vary |
| RS011 | [Global Mangrove Watch](https://www.globalmangrovewatch.org/) — Mangrove extent, change and alerts | Check indicator applicability at local scale |
| RS012 | [Allen Coral Atlas](https://allencoralatlas.org/) — Coral-reef habitat maps and monitoring | Attribution required; coverage and depth limits |
| RS013 | [JRC Global Surface Water](https://global-surface-water.appspot.com/) — Water occurrence, seasonality and change | GeoTIFF; custom analysis in GIS or Earth Engine; check release notes |
| RS014 | [GloFAS / Global Flood Monitoring](https://global-flood.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — Flood forecasts and satellite inundation | Forecasts and satellite observations are distinct |
| RS015 | [Copernicus Drought Observatories](https://drought.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — European and global drought indicators | Includes satellite, meteorological and model inputs |
| RS016 | [EFFIS](https://forest-fire.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — Fires, burned areas, danger and risk | Separate detected events, burned area and forecast danger |
| RS017 | [NASA FIRMS](https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/) — Active fires and thermal anomalies | CSV/KML/shapefile; hotspots are not burn boundaries |
| RS018 | [Copernicus Marine MyOcean Pro](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/viewer/expert) — Marine observations and models | Commonly NetCDF; distinguish model from observation |
| RS019 | [Global Human Settlement Layer](https://human-settlement.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — Built-up areas, settlements and population | Population is estimated; check product resolution |
| RS021 | [ICGC viewers and downloads](https://www.icgc.cat/en/Tools-and-viewers/Viewers) — Orthophotos, LiDAR and cartography | Includes airborne rather than satellite sensing |
| AMRKB context | Technical agricultural methods and management context | A method label provides context; ecological effects require observations and controlled comparison. |
| IoT (future) | Future calibrated environmental sensor datasets | Sensor depth/height, calibration, drift and gaps affect interpretation. |
| Bioinformatics (future) | Future biological observations and pipeline outputs | Sample support, controls, normalisation and reference databases affect interpretation. |


## Scientific references

These references support the stated definitions or framework connections. Specialist entries without an individual protocol citation remain working definitions. Specific inference limits are retained beside each indicator. Framework-defined thresholds require a stated version and regional justification.

| Key | Primary / authoritative reference | Documentary scope |
|---|---|---|
| R01 | [USGS — Landsat Enhanced Vegetation Index](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-enhanced-vegetation-index) | Standard EVI formula and band/scaling context; documentary check, not local validation. Relevant entries: Enhanced vegetation index (EVI). |
| R02 | [USGS — Landsat Normalized Burn Ratio](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-normalized-burn-ratio) | NBR formula and product context; not universal severity thresholds. Relevant entries: Burn ratio (NBR). |
| R03 | [FAO — SOC stock calculation sub-protocol, Annex 4](https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/GSP/MRV/GSP_MRV_Protocol_A4_EN_002.pdf) | SOC stock inputs and compatible density/coarse-fragment basis. Relevant entries: Soil organic carbon. |
| R04 | [EMBL-EBI — MGnify](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/about/teams/microbiome-informatics/mgnify/) | Taxonomic and functional-potential outputs, versioned pipelines; no project dataset accession bound. Relevant entries: Bacterial community, Archaeal community, Fungal community, Protist community, Carbon-breakdown genes, Microbial gene expression. |
| R05 | [Vandeputte et al. (2017) — Quantitative microbiome profiling](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature24460) | Primary study on relative versus quantitative abundance; gut study supports the compositional measurement caution, not soil-specific effect claims. Relevant entries: Bacterial community, Fungal:bacterial ratio, Microbial numbers. |
| R06 | [GEO BON — EBV strategy v2](https://geobon.org/downloads/governance-documents/Essential_Biodiversity_Variable_Strategy_v2.pdf) | Biodiversity observation framework; no claim that EII entries are certified EBVs. Relevant entries: Domain 6. |
| R07 | [WMO/GCOS — About Essential Climate Variables](https://gcos.wmo.int/site/global-climate-observing-system-gcos/essential-climate-variables/about-essential-climate-variables) | Climate observation framework; no one-to-one ECV crosswalk established. Relevant entries: Domain 1. |
| R08 | [UN — SEEA Ecosystem Accounting](https://seea.un.org/en/methodology/ecosystem-accounting) | Extent/condition/function accounting framework; EII composites remain locally specified. Relevant entries: Domain 11. |
| R09 | [Richardson et al. (2023) — Earth beyond six of nine planetary boundaries](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adh2458) | Historical framework reference for control-variable families; not a current boundary-status assessment or a local allocation method. Relevant entries: Domain 15. |
| R11 | [USGS — Normalized Difference Moisture Index](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/normalized-difference-moisture-index) | NIR/SWIR vegetation-moisture contrast and product context. Relevant entries: Canopy moisture index (NDMI). |
| R12 | [USGS — Scaling Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 Data](https://www.usgs.gov/software/scaling-landsat-collection-2-level-2-data) | Reflectance scaling before vegetation-index calculation and thermal conversion. Relevant entries: Vegetation greenness (NDVI). |
| R10 | [USGS — Dissolved Oxygen and Water](https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/dissolved-oxygen-and-water) | Dissolved oxygen as a water-quality variable and ecological context. Relevant entries: Dissolved oxygen. |

## Indicator families and distinct quantities

Some original labels group separate quantities under one stable ID. Select the appropriate component when recording measurements. Carbon concentration and stock, GPP and NPP, groundwater level and recharge, and conductivity and pH describe different quantities and must remain separate.

## Cross-domain questions

| Question | Helpful measurements | What to keep in mind |
|---|---|---|
| Are greener plants getting enough water? | Vegetation greenness, leaf area, soil moisture, plant water status and air humidity | Greenness can also change with plant type, leaf cover and nutrients. |
| Which terraces are losing soil? | Slope, terrace condition, erosion channels, vegetation cover, infiltration and rainfall | Terrain can suggest risk; measuring sediment or repeat ground change helps establish actual loss. |
| Is soil storing more carbon? | Soil carbon stock, soil density, stones/depth and repeated carbon measurements | Compare the same depth or soil mass. A higher carbon percentage alone is not proof of more stored carbon. |
| Does a farming method improve outcomes? | Crop yield, water and nitrogen use, soil structure/carbon, nutrient losses and pollinator visits | Compare similar treated and untreated areas over time. Look for trade-offs as well as benefits. |
| Are nitrogen-cycling genes linked to activity? | Genetic markers, gene expression, nitrogen transformation rates and gas measurements | Having a gene, expressing it and carrying out a process are different evidence steps. |
| Do habitat connections support movement? | Habitat maps, barriers, movement observations and population genetics | A mapped corridor is only a possible route until use is demonstrated. |
| Has an ecosystem recovered? | Plant species, population numbers, soil functions and production measured repeatedly | Green cover may return before the original species or functions recover. |
| Where could fire spread most easily? | Fuel amount/arrangement, dryness, wind, slope and fire history | Fuel and weather describe hazard; ignition and the people or habitats exposed also matter. |

Use ISO 8601 timestamps with timezone, explicit dry/wet and element/compound mass bases, documented units and named uncertainty models. Add sensors/calibration/drift/gaps for IoT; add sample/depth/accessions, extraction/primers, controls, library size, normalisation, annotation/reference versions and pipeline version for bioinformatics. Source routes above remain candidates; AMRKB should normally bind as `contextualised_by` or a separately identified technical method, not `observed_in`, until actual observations exist. A future dataset's namespace must be registered deliberately, rather than inferring a new database identity from the labels “IoT” or “bioinformatics”.\n\nFor actual computational dependencies, store `input_observation_ids` and the formula/pipeline independently of the inventory's interpretive `support`. A field-validated NDVI biomass model should bind both reflectance and calibration observations and declare an `estimated_by` relation; it must not relabel NDVI itself as measured biomass.\n\n### SOC stock calculation example\n\nUsing organic C concentration in g/kg, compatible fine-earth bulk density in g/cm³, layer thickness in cm and coarse-fragment volume fraction, a commonly used stock form is:\n\n`SOC stock (Mg C/ha) = C (g/kg) × BD_fine (g/cm³) × thickness (cm) × (1 − coarse_fragment_volume_fraction) × 0.1`.\n\nThe density denominator and fragment correction must match: do not apply the correction twice if density already expresses dry fine-earth mass per total sample volume. Sum declared layers; use consistent/equivalent soil mass for repeated comparisons where density changes. Concentration, stock and stock-change rate remain separate variants/records. [FAO Annex 4](https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/GSP/MRV/GSP_MRV_Protocol_A4_EN_002.pdf).\n\n## Appendix B — Scientific reference and verification register\n\nAll definitions are curated working entries. A citation verifies only the specific documentary aspect described below, not every inference, local calibration or monitoring protocol. Uncited entries remain pending individual literature/protocol review. Frameworks guide coverage and terminology; formal EBV/ECV/SEEA equivalence has not been asserted. The 2023 planetary-boundary paper is a versioned conceptual reference; this inventory reports no current number of transgressed boundaries, current threshold values or automatic local allocations.\n\n| Key | Primary/authoritative reference | Scope of documentary check |\n|---|---|---|\n| R01 | [USGS — Landsat Enhanced Vegetation Index](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-enhanced-vegetation-index) | Standard EVI formula and band/scaling context; documentary check, not local validation. |\n| R02 | [USGS — Landsat Normalized Burn Ratio](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-normalized-burn-ratio) | NBR formula and product context; not universal severity thresholds. |\n| R03 | [FAO — SOC stock calculation sub-protocol, Annex 4](https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/GSP/MRV/GSP_MRV_Protocol_A4_EN_002.pdf) | SOC stock inputs and compatible density/coarse-fragment basis. |\n| R04 | [EMBL-EBI — MGnify](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/about/teams/microbiome-informatics/mgnify/) | Taxonomic and functional-potential outputs, versioned pipelines; no project dataset accession bound. |\n| R05 | [Vandeputte et al. (2017) — Quantitative microbiome profiling](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature24460) | Primary study on relative versus quantitative abundance; gut study supports the compositional measurement caution, not soil-specific effect claims. |\n| R06 | [GEO BON — EBV strategy v2](https://geobon.org/downloads/governance-documents/Essential_Biodiversity_Variable_Strategy_v2.pdf) | Biodiversity observation framework; no claim that EII entries are certified EBVs. |\n| R07 | [WMO/GCOS — About Essential Climate Variables](https://gcos.wmo.int/site/global-climate-observing-system-gcos/essential-climate-variables/about-essential-climate-variables) | Climate observation framework; no one-to-one ECV crosswalk established. |\n| R08 | [UN — SEEA Ecosystem Accounting](https://seea.un.org/en/methodology/ecosystem-accounting) | Extent/condition/function accounting framework; EII composites remain locally specified. |\n| R09 | [Richardson et al. (2023) — Earth beyond six of nine planetary boundaries](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adh2458) | Historical framework reference for control-variable families; not a current boundary-status assessment or a local allocation method. |\n| R11 | [USGS — Normalized Difference Moisture Index](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/normalized-difference-moisture-index) | NIR/SWIR vegetation-moisture contrast and product context. |\n| R12 | [USGS — Scaling Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 Data](https://www.usgs.gov/software/scaling-landsat-collection-2-level-2-data) | Reflectance scaling before vegetation-index calculation and thermal conversion. |\n| R10 | [USGS — Dissolved Oxygen and Water](https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/dissolved-oxygen-and-water) | Dissolved oxygen as a water-quality variable and ecological context. |\n\nFramework coverage notes: D1 draws on climate observation concepts (R07); D6 covers biodiversity observations (R06); D11 retains extent/condition/function distinctions (R08); D15 lists empirical variables and framework-defined comparisons (R09). Boundary thresholds and ecological reference states remain model/framework choices requiring justification; they are not interchangeable universal measurements.\n\n## Appendix C — Cross-domain interpretation examples\n\n| Question | Indicator combination | Required qualification |\n|---|---|---|\n| Does a greener canopy indicate better water status? | VEG-001, VEG-011, VEG-013, HYD-001, VEG-020, ATM-003 | Separate leaf area, chlorophyll, water access and atmospheric demand; calibrate by species and season. |\n| Is carbon actually accumulating? | SOI-005 stock variant, SOI-002, SOI-014, FUN-002, CYC-001 | Repeat compatible stocks with uncertainty, account for depth/mass, export and gas fluxes; SOC % alone is insufficient. |\n| Are nitrogen-cycling genes expressing realised function? | MIC-010/011/012, MIC-022, MIC-023, CYC-004/005, CYC-002 | DNA → transcription → process are distinct observations; sample together and measure substrate/environment. |\n| Does a technical agricultural intervention improve outcomes? | AMRKB method context; FUN-004, AGR-001/002, SOI-003/005, HYD-018, BIO-008 | Compare matched controls over time; retain trade-offs and confounders rather than presuming benefit from a method label. |\n| Does mapped connectivity support biological movement? | BIO-007, LAN-004, BIO-015, INT-007, BIO-016 | Validate pathways with movement/genetic evidence and demographic context; spatial similarity is insufficient. |\n| Has a disturbed ecosystem recovered? | DIS-009, RES-001/002/005, VEG-017, BIO-002, FUN-001, MIC-024 | Use explicit reference conditions and multiple responses; greenness recovery alone is narrow evidence. |\n\n## Maintenance, validation and next review\n\nNew IDs are assigned once; edits preserve identity unless a concept changes enough to require a new record and explicit relation. Definitions and formulas must cite the selected convention; variant additions must not change old series meaning. New dataset links need actual source-system IDs and a resolved binding. Add new contributing scientific/technological catalogues to the route registry without duplicating their authoritative records or introducing excluded-project dependencies.\n\nBefore using an indicator operationally: select the variant and assay/product; confirm units and method version; validate context-specific inference; record uncertainty, spatial/temporal support and sampling design. For modelled/composite/predictive outputs, keep inputs, weights, baseline, validation and scenario explicit. Verify specialist entries against primary protocols during Stage B, prioritising molecular functions, composite indices, remote trait retrievals and threshold comparisons.\n\n### Version history\n\n- **0.2.0 — 13 October 2026:** Expanded the 120-record baseline into the 15-domain master register; retained every original ID and preferred label; added working definitions, observed inputs, units, qualified inferences, supporting-ID links and four-level classifications. Removed the excluded programme crosswalk and excluded interoperability dependencies. Added candidate GISDS source routes, scope-only AMRKB context, unresolved future channels, variant discipline, provenance hashes and schema validation.\n- **0.1.0 — 10 October 2026:** Original consolidated inventory; retained as the reviewed provenance baseline, including sections intentionally removed from this edition.\n",
    "register_v0_2_1_introduction": "# EII — Ecological Indicator Reference Register\n\nA reference to scientific and technological indicators of ecological condition, processes and environmental pressures. The register explains what each indicator represents, what is observed or calculated, which inferences it can support, and which other indicators help interpret it.\n\n## Reading the tables\n\nEach row names an indicator, explains how and where it is measured, and gives a short explanation of what it can tell us. Supporting indicators are clickable names for other measurements that help interpret the result.\n\nRS source references point to the source register below. IoT means connected environmental sensors; “future” means that the contributing dataset catalogue has not yet been connected. Source pointers are possibilities, so the exact dataset or field method still needs checking.\n\n",

Calculation, Model estimate | region, planet | year, decade | Large-scale pressure, Comparison with a threshold |\n\n## Observation methods and information products\n\n| Method / platform | Primary observations or products | Typical EII use | Main qualification |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| RGB drone, camera or orthophoto | Visible colour channels and mapped surface features | Vegetation cover, terraces, built geometry | Lighting, colour processing, scale and geometric accuracy affect comparisons. |\n| Multispectral / hyperspectral sensing | Reflectance at specified wavelengths | Greenness, pigment and moisture contrasts; calibrated traits | Band ratios directly describe spectra; physiology requires validation. No hyperspectral dataset was bound from GISDS. |\n| Thermal imaging | Thermal radiance and retrieved surface temperature | Surface heating and canopy temperature anomalies | Emissivity, atmosphere and acquisition time matter; surface temperature differs from air temperature. |\n| Satellite radar (SAR) | Backscatter/coherence and interpreted classifications | Inundation and surface-change screening | Moisture, roughness, vegetation and viewing geometry can produce similar signals. |\n| LiDAR / structure-from-motion | Point clouds, terrain and surface models | Height, crown geometry, terrain and repeat change | Ground classification, co-registration and occlusion affect results; geometry is not biomass directly. |\n| Weather / hydrology stations and future IoT | Temperature, rainfall, humidity, flow and calibrated sensor streams | Climate, water balance, exposure and event monitoring | Record sensor calibration, depth/height, gaps, drift and temporal support. |\n| Soil / water laboratory assays | Carbon, nutrients, chemistry and physical properties | Pools, concentrations, contamination and retention | Extraction, dry/wet basis, detection limits and compatible units must be declared. |\n| Field ecological surveys | Organisms, abundance, traits, visits and demographic observations | Biodiversity, interactions and population change | Sampling effort and imperfect detection constrain inference. |\n| Amplicon / shotgun sequencing | Marker sequences, taxonomic profiles and encoded genes | Community composition and genetic potential | Relative reads are not absolute abundance; DNA potential is not expression or process flux. |\n| RNA, proteins and metabolites | Transcripts, detected proteins and metabolite pools | Biochemical state and activity-related evidence | These evidence layers remain distinct; pools/signals do not directly measure realised flux. |\n| Controlled process assays / flux measurements | Transformation, growth, respiration or exchange rates | Nitrogen cycling, decomposition and carbon balances | Assay conditions and field representativeness determine applicability. |\n\n## Source register\n\n| Source ref | Resource / contribution | Interpretation note |\n|---|---|---|\n| RS001 | [Copernicus Browser](https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/) — Satellite imagery and indices | GeoTIFF; raw versus rendered export matters |\n| RS002 | [USGS EarthExplorer](https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov/) — Landsat reflectance and temperature | Follow product scaling and quality masks |\n| RS004 | [Copernicus Land Monitoring Service](https://land.copernicus.eu/en) — Land cover and environmental variables | Check resolution, period and product documentation |\n| RS005 | [ESA WorldCover](https://viewer.esa-worldcover.org/) — 10 m land-cover maps: 2020 and 2021 | Algorithms differ between years; GeoTIFF and QGIS styles |\n| RS006 | [Dynamic World](https://www.dynamicworld.app/) — 10 m land-cover classes and probabilities | Per-observation classification varies with conditions |\n| RS009 | [MapBiomas](https://mapbiomas.org/) — Annual land-cover and land-use maps | Coverage, collections and methods vary |\n| RS011 | [Global Mangrove Watch](https://www.globalmangrovewatch.org/) — Mangrove extent, change and alerts | Check indicator applicability at local scale |\n| RS012 | [Allen Coral Atlas](https://allencoralatlas.org/) — Coral-reef habitat maps and monitoring | Attribution required; coverage and depth limits |\n| RS013 | [JRC Global Surface Water](https://global-surface-water.appspot.com/) — Water occurrence, seasonality and change | GeoTIFF; custom analysis in GIS or Earth Engine; check release notes |\n| RS014 | [GloFAS / Global Flood Monitoring](https://global-flood.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — Flood forecasts and satellite inundation | Forecasts and satellite observations are distinct |\n| RS015 | [Copernicus Drought Observatories](https://drought.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — European and global drought indicators | Includes satellite, meteorological and model inputs |\n| RS016 | [EFFIS](https://forest-fire.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — Fires, burned areas, danger and risk | Separate detected events, burned area and forecast danger |\n| RS017 | [NASA FIRMS](https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/) — Active fires and thermal anomalies | CSV/KML/shapefile; hotspots are not burn boundaries |\n| RS018 | [Copernicus Marine MyOcean Pro](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/viewer/expert) — Marine observations and models | Commonly NetCDF; distinguish model from observation |\n| RS019 | [Global Human Settlement Layer](https://human-settlement.emergency.copernicus.eu/) — Built-up areas, settlements and population | Population is estimated; check product resolution |\n| RS021 | [ICGC viewers and downloads](https://www.icgc.cat/en/Tools-and-viewers/Viewers) — Orthophotos, LiDAR and cartography | Includes airborne rather than satellite sensing |\n| AMRKB context | Technical agricultural methods and management context | A method label provides context; ecological effects require observations and controlled comparison. |\n| IoT (future) | Future calibrated environmental sensor datasets | Sensor depth/height, calibration, drift and gaps affect interpretation. |\n| Bioinformatics (future) | Future biological observations and pipeline outputs | Sample support, controls, normalisation and reference databases affect interpretation. |\n\n\n## Scientific references\n\nThese references support the stated definitions or framework connections. Specialist entries without an individual protocol citation remain working definitions. Specific inference limits are retained beside each indicator. Framework-defined thresholds require a stated version and regional justification.\n\n| Key | Primary / authoritative reference | Documentary scope |\n|---|---|---|\n| R01 | [USGS — Landsat Enhanced Vegetation Index](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-enhanced-vegetation-index) | Standard EVI formula and band/scaling context; documentary check, not local validation. Relevant entries: Enhanced vegetation index (EVI). |\n| R02 | [USGS — Landsat Normalized Burn Ratio](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-normalized-burn-ratio) | NBR formula and product context; not universal severity thresholds. Relevant entries: Burn ratio (NBR). |\n| R03 | [FAO — SOC stock calculation sub-protocol, Annex 4](https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/GSP/MRV/GSP_MRV_Protocol_A4_EN_002.pdf) | SOC stock inputs and compatible density/coarse-fragment basis. Relevant entries: Soil organic carbon. |\n| R04 | [EMBL-EBI — MGnify](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/about/teams/microbiome-informatics/mgnify/) | Taxonomic and functional-potential outputs, versioned pipelines; no project dataset accession bound. Relevant entries: Bacterial community, Archaeal community, Fungal community, Protist community, Carbon-breakdown genes, Microbial gene expression. |\n| R05 | [Vandeputte et al. (2017) — Quantitative microbiome profiling](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature24460) | Primary study on relative versus quantitative abundance; gut study supports the compositional measurement caution, not soil-specific effect claims. Relevant entries: Bacterial community, Fungal:bacterial ratio, Microbial numbers. |\n| R06 | [GEO BON — EBV strategy v2](https://geobon.org/downloads/governance-documents/Essential_Biodiversity_Variable_Strategy_v2.pdf) | Biodiversity observation framework; no claim that EII entries are certified EBVs. Relevant entries: Domain 6. |\n| R07 | [WMO/GCOS — About Essential Climate Variables](https://gcos.wmo.int/site/global-climate-observing-system-gcos/essential-climate-variables/about-essential-climate-variables) | Climate observation framework; no one-to-one ECV crosswalk established. Relevant entries: Domain 1. |\n| R08 | [UN — SEEA Ecosystem Accounting](https://seea.un.org/en/methodology/ecosystem-accounting) | Extent/condition/function accounting framework; EII composites remain locally specified. Relevant entries: Domain 11. |\n| R09 | [Richardson et al. (2023) — Earth beyond six of nine planetary boundaries](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adh2458) | Historical framework reference for control-variable families; not a current boundary-status assessment or a local allocation method. Relevant entries: Domain 15. |\n| R11 | [USGS — Normalized Difference Moisture Index](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/normalized-difference-moisture-index) | NIR/SWIR vegetation-moisture contrast and product context. Relevant entries: Canopy moisture index (NDMI). |\n| R12 | [USGS — Scaling Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 Data](https://www.usgs.gov/software/scaling-landsat-collection-2-level-2-data) | Reflectance scaling before vegetation-index calculation and thermal conversion. Relevant entries: Vegetation greenness (NDVI). |\n| R10 | [USGS — Dissolved Oxygen and Water](https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/dissolved-oxygen-and-water) | Dissolved oxygen as a water-quality variable and ecological context. Relevant entries: Dissolved oxygen. |\n\n## Indicator families and distinct quantities\n\nSome original labels group separate quantities under one stable ID. | mortality rate, recruitment rate |\n| <small>[AGR-005 — Crop disease incidence and severity](#agr-005)</small> | disease incidence, disease severity |\n| <small>[AGR-009 — Forage use and imported feed](#agr-009)</small> | forage utilisation, imported feed share |\n| <small>[AGR-011 — Farm nutrient and energy balance](#agr-011)</small> | nutrient balance, energy balance |\n| <small>[HUM-003 — Material use and recycling](#hum-003)</small> | material flow, recycled input fraction |\n| <small>[HUM-004 — Energy demand and return](#hum-004)</small> | energy demand, energy return ratio |\n| <small>[HUM-005 — Water withdrawal and consumption](#hum-005)</small> | water withdrawal, water consumption |\n| <small>[PB-001 — Global carbon dioxide and climate forcing](#pb-001)</small> | CO2 concentration, radiative forcing |\n| <small>[PB-002 — Large-scale biodiversity and function loss](#pb-002)</small> | genetic integrity control, functional integrity control |\n| <small>[PB-003 — Large-scale nitrogen and phosphorus pressures](#pb-003)</small> | N control, P control |\n| <small>[PB-004 — Large-scale river-flow and soil-moisture change](#pb-004)</small> | blue water change, green water change |\n\n## Cross-domain questions\n\n| Question | Helpful measurements | What to keep in mind |\n|---|---|---|\n| Are greener plants getting enough water? | Vegetation greenness, leaf area, soil moisture, plant water status and air humidity | Greenness can also change with plant type, leaf cover and nutrients. |\n| Which terraces are losing soil? | Slope, terrace condition, erosion channels, vegetation cover, infiltration and rainfall | Terrain can suggest risk; measuring sediment or repeat ground change helps establish actual loss. |\n| Is soil storing more carbon? | Soil carbon stock, soil density, stones/depth and repeated carbon measurements | Compare the same depth or soil mass. A higher carbon percentage alone is not proof of more stored carbon. |\n| Does a farming method improve outcomes? | Crop yield, water and nitrogen use, soil structure/carbon, nutrient losses and pollinator visits | Compare similar treated and untreated areas over time. Look for trade-offs as well as benefits. |\n| Are nitrogen-cycling genes linked to activity? | Genetic markers, gene expression, nitrogen transformation rates and gas measurements | Having a gene, expressing it and carrying out a process are different evidence steps. |\n| Do habitat connections support movement? | Habitat maps, barriers, movement observations and population genetics | A mapped corridor is only a possible route until use is demonstrated. |\n| Has an ecosystem recovered? | Plant species, population numbers, soil functions and production measured repeatedly | Green cover may return before the original species or functions recover. |\n| Where could fire spread most easily? | Fuel amount/arrangement, dryness, wind, slope and fire history | Fuel and weather describe hazard; ignition and the people or habitats exposed also matter. |\n",
    "machine_readme_v0_2_1": "# EII reference register — machine README\n\n**Work in Progress — Academic Research Resource**\n\nAuthor: Jonathan Minchin · Ecological Interaction · [ORCID 0000-0001-8152-1796](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8152-1796).\n\nStart with the [Ecological Indicator Reference Register](EII_Reference_Register.md). The [remote-sensing subset](EII%20-%20Remote%20Sensing.md) provides a focused reading view; [EII.md](EII.md) preserves the extended inventory baseline. Citation metadata is in [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff), and publication preparation is recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).\n\n## Two maintained files\n\n- `EII_Reference_Register.md`: the human-readable scientific register. Its tables contain all 235 indicators, the original 15 domains, direct measurements/calculations, inference limits, supporting indicators, classifications, methods, concise source pointers and scientific references.\n- `README.md`: administrative history, update workflow, interoperability rules, schema, baseline provenance and a complete machine-readable snapshot. This is the technical companion, not an additional indicator inventory.\n\nBoth files are intended to be maintained together. There is no automatic synchronization with repository EII.md, GISDS, AMRKB or remote services. The working pair is installed in the EII repository folder. `EII_Reference_Register.md` is the human reading interface and this `README.md` is its machine-oriented companion. The existing `EII.md` remains the earlier inventory baseline; future register work should maintain the two files named above together.\n\n## Versions and changes\n\n**Pair version:** 0.2.1. **Scientific inventory baseline:** extended EII v0.2.0. **Created:** 13 October 2026.\n\n- EII v0.1.0 provided 120 stable IDs and labels across eight compilation groups.\n- EII v0.2.0 expanded this to 235 records in the agreed 15 domains, adding operational definitions, units/formulas, qualified inferences, support links, classifications and candidate source routes.\n- The v0.2.1 presentation converted these entries to human-readable tables without changing the inventory's scientific content.\n- This new two-file register uses the complete extended v0.2.0 record set and the table presentation. Administrative sections, editorial roadmap, provenance hashes, technical variants and machine data are moved here. The human file retains scientific limitations, since those are essential to interpreting the indicators.\n- Pair v0.2.0 simplifies the main register to five columns: indicator, measurement/source, beginner inference, supporting indicator names and concise sources. Visible EII IDs, coded kind/method columns, indicator definitions and dagger markers are removed from the main reading view. Stable IDs, canonical labels, rigorous definitions and detailed inferences remain in the machine snapshot; names link through stable anchors. Both deliverables remain Markdown.\n\n### Reference display update — pair v0.2.1\n\nEach indicator now displays its short stable reference beside its existing beginner-facing name, for example **MIC-005 — Microbial diversity within a sample**. The same references are restored in the left columns of the classification and indicator-family tables. The human names, measurements, inferences, supporting links and source pointers remain unchanged.\n\nThe register still has five main columns: no separate ID or coded kind/method column is added. Main-table first-column reference/name text and last-column Sources text use HTML `<small>`; the middle columns retain the normal text size. Bold reference/name text uses `<strong>` inside `<small>`. Markdown has no native per-column font-size control, so visual sizing depends on the renderer supporting these HTML tags; readers that strip them still retain the references and content.\n\n`display_reference` stores the short ID. `display_reference_label` stores the combined short ID/name. `display_column_sizes` records the presentation intent. The preserved `id`, canonical label/definition/measurement/inference fields, beginner display fields, classifications, source routes and all other record metadata remain intact. The manifest stores the previous presentation state in `presentation_history` and the current display rule in `presentation`.\n\nFor future edits, add or preserve the short reference in the left cell, keep its stable anchor unchanged, and retain the smaller first/last-column wrappers. An indicator name change must update `display_label` and `display_reference_label`; an identity change requires an explicit stable-ID decision, not a cosmetic rename. Refresh the human hash after saving.\n\nThe files use stable names; future versions belong inside this README rather than new filename suffixes. The human register contains no version history, implementation schema, raw JSON registry, workflow, audit hashes or file-system provenance.\n\n## Update workflow\n\n1. Read both files and identify the affected stable EII IDs. Treat human table content as the editorial interface for labels, definitions, measurements and inferences; treat this README as the operational metadata and synchronization companion.\n2. Edit the scientific row and any associated classification, family description, source or reference row. Keep definitions, measurements, potential functions and realised process rates distinct. Preserve original labels/IDs unless an explicitly justified scientific correction is recorded here.\n3. Update the matching JSON record below in the same change. Human field mapping: the hidden stable anchor identifies `id`; indicator name → `display_label`; measurement/source text → `display_measurement`, `measurement_origin` and canonical `direct`; beginner inference → `display_inference`; named supporting links → `support`; concise sources → `display_source_refs` and resolved `routes`. Keep canonical `label`, `definition` and detailed `inference` alongside the beginner fields; do not silently discard their scientific distinctions. There is no visible kind/method code column.\n4. For an operational-metadata change, update this README and refresh any affected human source pointer, classification or quantity distinction. Do not expand human rows with acquisition schemas, raw accessions, large JSON or administrative notes.\n5. If either file has diverged, compare values by stable ID and reconcile both explicitly. Do not silently regenerate one from a stale snapshot. The machine snapshot is synchronized data, not permission to overwrite later human edits.\n6. New records receive an unused ID, one home domain, non-empty definition/direct/inference fields, and appropriate classifications. IDs are never recycled or renumbered when domains change. Retain a redirect/versioned reason if a concept is merged or retired.\n7. Validate the pair: unique IDs; all original 120 IDs/labels preserved unless an explicit correction is recorded; 15 domains; support links and anchors resolve; route/ref keys resolve; no excluded interoperability edges; family quantities remain separate; complete matching row/record sets.\n8. Record the substantive update and evidence-review scope here. Refresh the human-file SHA-256 in the manifest after saving. Keep source-review hashes labelled as baseline provenance, rather than treating them as current remote or repository state.\n\n## Scope and scientific review state\n\nOnly scientific/technological indicators and empirically describable pressures/context are in scope. Exclude the Trails4Soil practice list/crosswalk and all interoperability dependencies to PBCKA or EIRKB. AMRKB can provide technical agricultural methods and management context, not philosophical/cultural classification. Quantitative resource flows and human environmental pressures remain in Domain 14.\n\nAll records are curated working definitions. `refs` indicates a documentary source for a specific aspect, not full local validation or certification. `review_scope: specific_documentary_aspects_only` must not be upgraded to a verified standard without a protocol-level review. Framework references do not assert a formal EBV/ECV/SEEA crosswalk. The planetary-boundary source is a versioned framework reference, not a current transgression count or automatic local threshold allocation.\n\nSupporting indicators are directed interpretive recommendations, not necessarily calculation dependencies or causal evidence. `input_observation_ids` belongs to actual computations and must be stored separately from `support`. Increased greenness, diversity, respiration or composite score is not universally a beneficial outcome. Composite/predictive/modelled records require declared inputs, conventions, baselines, uncertainty and validation.\n\n## Identifier and field contract\n\n- `id`: full stable identifier `EII:VEG-001`; its short form is now visible beside the indicator name, and its lowercase form remains the stable link anchor. There is no separate ID column. Prefix does not encode current domain.\n- `label`, `definition`, `direct`, `inference`: preserved detailed scientific layer from the extended inventory. Human names, measurements and inferences have their own display fields; definitions are retained here rather than appended to indicator names.\n- `domain`: D01–D15, one home domain. `related_domains`: optional cross-domain associations without record duplication.\n- `secondary`: evidence/acquisition tags (`observed`, `measured`, `derived`, `proxy`, `inferred`, `modelled`, `composite`, `predictive`, `process`, `context`, `pressure`).\n- `tertiary.spatial` / `tertiary.temporal`: typical applicability, not native resolution or validated extrapolation.\n- `quaternary`: ecological/assessment role; provisional and method-dependent.\n- `support`: full EII IDs for interpretive companion indicators.\n- `routes`: EII-local route keys resolved in the manifest; these are not invented source-system records.\n- `refs`: local EII scientific reference keys R01–R12, resolved to title/URL/scope in the manifest and human reference table.\n- `record_type`: `indicator` or `family`. `variants`: stable quantity keys under a family ID. Observations of families must identify the selected variant.\n- `status`, `review_scope`, `legacy`: review/migration metadata retained here rather than in reader-facing rows.\n- `display_label`: short human-readable indicator name, which may differ from the preserved canonical label.\n- `measurement_origin`, `display_measurement`: plain acquisition source and reader-facing measurement text; source describes satellite, sensor, field, laboratory, records or model as appropriate.\n- `display_inference`: beginner-facing explanation with essential limitations retained; canonical `inference` preserves fuller scientific detail.\n- `display_source_refs`: concise source pointers without dagger markers.\n- `display_kind`: null because the coded column is removed. `display_methods` retains the former acquisition codes for audit/migration only; it is not shown as a main-table column.\n\n## Interoperability and unresolved routes\n\nExisting GISDS catalogue IDs RS001–RS022 remain authoritative in GISDS; only relevant reviewed IDs are referenced here. A platform/resource is not a dataset. Route links are candidates until exact product, dataset, release, location/date, processing, licence and calibration are bound. Not every hosted product is suitable for every indicator. Red-edge retrieval requires the appropriate bands; thermal estimates require thermal observations; ground models differ from canopy surface models.\n\nAMRKB v0.1.0 is a scope/architecture document with no implemented record IDs or observation database found. Its routes express technical method/management context, not data provenance. Future IoT and bioinformatics channels have null namespaces and null dataset IDs; no existing database identity, accession or sensor stream is implied. Discovery tools, rendered maps, AI summaries and computation services do not replace original observation provenance.\n\nObservation relations are controlled: `observed_in`, `derived_from`, `estimated_by`, `contextualised_by`, `processed_by`, `supported_by`. AMRKB normally binds as `contextualised_by` until actual observations/method IDs exist. Cross-catalogue updates are explicit; do not duplicate or overwrite authoritative GISDS/AMRKB catalogues.\n\n## Observation binding template\n\nStore actual observations in contributing datasets. This unfilled template is not a measurement or a completed source binding. Null means unknown/unbound, not zero; censored non-detects and missing data are distinct.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"eii_id\": \"EII:SOI-005\",\n  \"variant\": \"organic_C_stock\",\n  \"observation_id\": null,\n  \"binding_status\": \"unbound\",\n  \"source_namespace\": null,\n  \"source_record_id\": null,\n  \"dataset_id\": null,\n  \"dataset_version\": null,\n  \"relation\": \"derived_from\",\n  \"method_id\": null,\n  \"method_version\": null,\n  \"value\": null,\n  \"unit\": \"Mg C/ha\",\n  \"location_id\": null,\n  \"geometry\": null,\n  \"crs\": null,\n  \"spatial_support\": null,\n  \"depth_interval_cm\": null,\n  \"time_start\": null,\n  \"time_end\": null,\n  \"input_observation_ids\": [],\n  \"processing\": null,\n  \"calibration\": null,\n  \"uncertainty\": null,\n  \"quality_flags\": [],\n  \"detection_limit\": null,\n  \"licence\": null,\n  \"attribution\": null,\n  \"retrieved_at\": null\n}\n```\n\nUse ISO 8601 timestamps with timezones. Record actual support, depth and period, compatible units, dry/wet and element/compound mass bases. For IoT, retain sensor identity, calibration, drift, gaps and sampling interval. For biological observations, retain sample/depth/accessions, extraction/primers, controls, library coverage, normalization, annotation/reference release and pipeline version. Field-calibrated model estimates bind their observations and validation separately from the underlying index.\n\nSOC concentration, stock and stock change remain separate quantities. A compatible stock calculation uses concentration, density, thickness and coarse-fragment correction; do not double-correct a density already expressed as fine-earth mass per total sample volume. Repeated stock comparisons must address depth/equivalent soil mass and uncertainty. Other family components likewise retain distinct methods and units.\n\n## Manifest and source-route registry\n\nThe manifest describes this pair and the reviewed baseline. Paths/hashes identify reference material already read; they do not establish current remote content or live synchronization. The human hash covers the saved UTF-8 human register.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"pair_version\": \"0.2.1\",\n  \"inventory_content_version\": \"0.2.0\",\n  \"created\": \"2026-10-13\",\n  \"human_file\": \"EII_Reference_Register.md\",\n  \"machine_file\": \"README.md\",\n  \"human_format\": \"markdown_tables\",\n  \"schema_version\": \"eii.reference-register/1.0\",\n  \"record_count\": 235,\n  \"domain_count\": 15,\n  \"legacy_record_count\": 120,\n  \"new_record_count\": 115,\n  \"review_status\": \"curated_working_definitions_with_scoped_documentary_checks\",\n  \"human_file_sha256\": \"584c961895a334b695ee9f39fe98dcfa8c1385f8c8c02b143d29352c4780ccb3\",\n  \"baseline_source_review\": [\n    {\n      \"path\": \"/Users/jonathan/Github/ecological-information/EII/EII.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"47f7098f999cbb2570464d198793a11b0624386ee9b43fad0a2e9edd3451d547\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"/Users/jonathan/Github/ecological-information/EII/README.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"41429e550fc7fb4ccc313543f320a8e14df49bfcab5881e7137061ebf0bb0d92\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"/Users/jonathan/Github/ecological-information/GISDS/Cartography_Database_Sources.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"82cec11c4eb6706ac200db2986631c3e25831ae6424f3b955e4bcfa0813ec1b8\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"/Users/jonathan/Github/ecological-information/GISDS/README.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"84b225b53b0999c4d46144e7436f93560ddbf29d79e587ad7bbd38e9f2ab3a8c\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"/Users/jonathan/Github/ecological-information/AMRKB/README.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"4eb11eb8f9ead8d907007dc26d0c469d8dda78b1d250b9dab1b9205d10708ea1\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"derived_from\": {\n    \"path\": \"inventory.json\",\n    \"sha256\": \"d74303fde9e19d2143a29bbb8168790f40945cfdece7c67d193ad7ee5ab9ae08\"\n  },\n  \"presentation_reference\": {\n    \"path\": \"GISDS/Cartography_Database_Sources.md\",\n    \"format\": \"human-oriented tables;
